# ADR-002: PostgreSQL as the system of record

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-09-11

## Context

The data is relational to its core: assemblies contain components,
revisions belong to components, measurements belong to test runs which
belong to experiments and subjects. Traceability queries are joins and
recursive walks. Some data (caliber specification, per-component
dimensions, measurement payloads) is semi-structured and evolves.

## Decision

PostgreSQL 16 is the only database. We use:

* UUID primary keys generated by the application.
* `JSONB` for semi-structured, evolving attributes (`Caliber.specification`,
  `ComponentRevision.dimensions`, later `Measurement.payload`). A key is
  promoted to a typed column when it is queried, validated or aggregated.
* `NUMERIC` for engineering quantities (millimetres, grams, degrees) —
  never floating point for anything that appears on a drawing.
* Lifecycle states stored as strings with check constraints rather than
  native enums, so adding a state is an ordinary migration.
* Recursive CTEs where BOM depth matters; application-level recursion where
  clarity matters more (watch BOMs are small).
* Alembic migrations, hand-reviewed, one per slice.

Local development and tests run against a real PostgreSQL in Docker
Compose; there is no SQLite mode. Tests apply the Alembic migrations, so
migration drift is caught by the test suite.

## Consequences

* One database engine to know well.
* No ORM-portability tax: we can use Postgres features freely.
* Backups are `pg_dump`. Files are elsewhere (ADR-003).
